reasons: Status can be set directly, bypassing workflow checks.

terms.meaning: The plan describing what a survey should cover.
A survey that is still being prepared and has not gone out.
A number showing how ready a survey is, from the validation checks.
A fixed list of fields that are permitted to change.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and router setup
sections.what: Brings in the web framework tools, database session, survey data types and date tools, then creates the router for survey routes.
sections.why: Likely reason: the main app needs one router object for these routes.

sections.name: SurveyCreate
sections.title: New survey request fields
sections.what: Describes a new survey: name, optional description, audience type and optional spec.
sections.why: Likely reason: the spec is optional so a survey can be created before planning.
sections.watch_out: The spec is free-form and is not checked here.

sections.name: SurveyResponse
sections.title: Survey summary returned
sections.what: Defines the fields returned for a survey, including ID, name, audience, status, creation time and Qualtrics links.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a user see the publish state at a glance.
sections.watch_out: The Qualtrics fields stay empty until publishing has happened.

sections.name: create_survey
sections.title: Create a new survey
sections.what: Creates a draft survey with a generated ID and returns its summary with a 201 created status.
sections.why: Likely reason: drafts keep unreviewed surveys from going out.
sections.watch_out: The creator is fixed to system with a TODO.

sections.name: get_survey
sections.title: Fetch one survey
sections.what: Returns the summary for a survey ID, or a not found error.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: get_survey_guide
sections.title: Full survey details
sections.what: Returns the spec, sections, validation results and readiness score for a survey in one response.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives one place to review everything about a survey.
sections.watch_out: Sections are returned as last saved. Nothing here checks that they still match the spec.

sections.name: update_survey
sections.title: Edit survey fields
sections.what: Changes only the name, description, spec, sections and status fields, then records the update time.
sections.why: Likely reason: an allowed list stops callers from changing other fields such as the ID.
sections.watch_out: Status is editable, so a caller can mark a survey published or approved without the workflow checks.

summary: Defines the web addresses for creating, reading, reviewing and editing survey records.
purpose: Lets a user create a survey, look it up, see its full details, and change selected fields.
why: Likely reason: new surveys start as drafts so that nothing goes out before review.
how: Defines request and response shapes. Creating saves a draft. Reading looks up the stored record. The guide route returns the spec, sections and checks together. Updating changes only the allowed fields.
inputs: Survey name, description, audience type, optional spec, a survey ID, and a dictionary of fields to update.
outputs: Survey summaries, a full guide with spec, sections, validation results and readiness score, and a success message after an update.
risks: Status is an editable field, so a caller can set a survey to approved or published without the workflow checks. Spec is not validated. The creator is fixed to system.
debug: If a survey is missing, check the ID. If the guide shows no sections, the workflow may not have finished. If a status change looks wrong, check the update route first.
